entry.title: RAW → Harmonization → Reporting: Where should Business Logic live?
entry.content:
A common approach is:
RAW → HARMONIZATION → REPORTING → SAC

On paper, this separation looks straightforward. But in real implementation projects, the boundaries between these layers can become less obvious.

One question I’ve been thinking about while working with SAP Datasphere: Where should business logic actually live in Raw, Harmonization, or Reporting?

For example:
COGS should be calculated from specific GL accounts, with sign inversion and certain account mappings applied.

Would you typically implement that logic in the HARMONIZATION layer, so it becomes reusable across multiple reports?

Or would you keep harmonization closer to the source data and implement the business rule in the REPORTING/Analytical Model layer, where it is directly tied to the reporting requirement?

I'm particularly interested in real project experience here.

Have you encountered cases where putting business logic in the wrong layer caused problems later, such as duplicated logic, inconsistent KPIs, performance issues, or having to redesign the model close to go-live?

Are there any Datasphere-specific limitations or best practices that influence where you place this logic?

Would love to hear how others approach this in actual implementations.

Thanks.

entry.title: Workflow for Journal entry verification - No Processor
entry.content:
Hello Community,

We're trying to activate the standard workflow for journal entry verification for our client in SAP S/4HANA Private cloud.

After doing the setup for the "Manage Workflows for Journal Entry Verification - For General Ledgers" and setting up the Team in "Manage Teams and Responsibilities for Journal Entries Verification". 

We tried to post an entry through the "Verify General Journal Entries - For Requester" to trigger the workflow.

Until here, everything is fine, we fill the needed information and click on "Post" and the message appears as the journal entry is submitted.

The issue is the following, even though we have setup the team, the workflow processor is always empty, the workflow is triggered but obviously blocked as there is no one to approve/reject in the processor. 

We went to the Tcode SWIA to analyze the logs, we see that it's like the workflow doesn't recognize the team yet we have maintained it correctly with the correct function which is matching the workflow set in place.

We already went through the note Notes - SAP for Me 3449877 and implemented the change but yet this is not the solution needed.

Can you please support on this ? 

Thanks & regards,

OS

entry.title: OB89 – Different G/L Account for Post Tax Payables in Portugal Depending on Company Code
entry.content:
Hello everyone,

We are configuring the Post Tax Payables functionality in the Run Statutory Reports app.

In transaction OB89, the G/L account used for the tax settlement posting is maintained in the account determination configuration. Currently, the same account is determined based on the chart of accounts.

However, we have a requirement to use a different G/L account for the Portuguese company code, while keeping the existing account for the other company codes.

For example:

  • Spanish company code: The current G/L account maintained in OB89 should continue to be used.

  • Portuguese company code: A different G/L account must be used for the tax settlement posting, in accordance with the Portuguese company's accounting requirements.

Both company codes use the same operational chart of accounts, so maintaining different accounts by chart of accounts does not meet our requirements. The account needs to be determined according to the company code.

My question is:

Is there a standard SAP configuration that allows us to determine a different G/L account for Post Tax Payables in OB89 depending on the company code?

If this is not possible directly in OB89, what is the recommended SAP approach to ensure that the Portuguese company code uses its specific G/L account while the other company codes continue using the existing account?

Thank you for your help.

entry.title: RE-FX Considerations During Subsequent Implementation of a Further Accounting Principle (SIL)
entry.content:
Hello SAP Community,

We are preparing a Subsequent Implementation of a Further Accounting Principle (SIL) in an existing production SAP S/4HANA environment to introduce a new US GAAP parallel ledger.

Only a subset of US company codes is included in the SIL project, and some of these company codes actively use Flexible Real Estate Management (RE-FX).

According to SAP documentation, “the subsequent implementation of a further accounting principle isn't supported for Flexible Real Estate Management (RE-FX).” Based on our discussions with SAP Support, we also understand that RE-FX postings should be avoided during the implementation year until SIL is completed to prevent potential inconsistencies during data transfer.

Our main question is how this restriction should be interpreted in practice. Does RE-FX activity need to be stopped from the beginning of the fiscal year until SIL completion, or only during the actual SIL execution window?

We would also like to understand what exactly is affected by this limitation. Are FI postings generated from RE-FX correctly transferred to the new ledger, or are there specific restrictions related to contracts, cash flows, valuations, or periodic postings?

For productive systems where stopping RE-FX activity for an extended period is not feasible, what mitigation approach is recommended? For example, can periodic postings be temporarily stopped and executed after SIL completion, or are additional reconciliation or adjustment activities required?

Finally, has anyone successfully completed SIL with RE-FX company codes in scope? We would particularly appreciate any experience regarding project sequencing, alternative approaches, or relevant SAP Notes and official documentation.

Thank you in advance for sharing your experience.

entry.title: SIL in Production: Customizing Changes, Error Handling and Recovery
entry.content:
Hello SAP Community,

We are preparing a Subsequent Implementation of a Further Accounting Principle (SIL) in an existing production SAP S/4HANA environment to introduce a new US GAAP parallel ledger.

Only a subset of US company codes is included in the SIL scope, while other company codes continue operating in the same production system. This makes a full production freeze or system restore particularly challenging.

One of our main questions concerns Customizing changes during the SIL project. Which configuration changes are actually monitored by SIL? Can unrelated transports continue to production, or is a broader Customizing freeze recommended until the project is completed?

We would also like to understand the practical error-handling options during productive execution. If issues occur during data transfer—for example, affecting ACDOCA, Asset Accounting, open items, or balances—can individual activities be corrected and reprocessed, or are manual adjustments required?

Our biggest concern is the recovery strategy. Once data transfer has started, is there any supported rollback mechanism if significant reconciliation issues are identified, or would recovery ultimately require a system restore?

In a global production environment, restoring the entire system would also affect company codes outside the SIL scope. Therefore, we are particularly interested in whether a forward-recovery approach is possible: correcting residual differences after the transfer rather than rolling back the complete SIL implementation.

If anyone has completed SIL in a productive S/4HANA system, we would greatly appreciate any experience regarding Customizing governance, error recovery, rollback versus forward recovery, and any relevant SAP Notes or official documentation.

Thank you in advance for sharing your experience.
